title: QUIC ngtcp2 Response Packet-Number Opening Verification
verification_method: Captured ngtcp2 packet replay, focused captured interop replay suite, and local quic-interop-runner ngtcp2 handshake rerun.
preconditions: The managed client has 1-RTT open material.
The Application Data receive packet-number state has advanced enough to reconstruct a one-byte truncated peer packet number.
The captured ngtcp2 packet uses TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 and the preserved SERVER_TRAFFIC_SECRET_0 from the local run key log.
scope: Verify the representative ngtcp2 post-handshake response liveness failure by proving the captured response packet opens only when the full packet number is reconstructed before AEAD nonce construction, and by rerunning the local handshake cell to successful completion.
procedure: Run the captured interop replay test class.
Confirm the captured ngtcp2 response packet fails without an expected packet number and opens with expected packet number 399463276.
Run the local quic-interop-runner helper with Incursa.Quic as client, ngtcp2 as server, and the handshake testcase.
Confirm the managed client reads the 1024-byte response and the runner reports the handshake testcase as succeeded.
expected_result: The captured ngtcp2 response packet authenticates and parses as ACK plus FIN-bearing STREAM data when the reconstructed packet number is used for the AEAD nonce, and the local ngtcp2 handshake cell succeeds.
evidence: pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/interop/Invoke-QuicInteropRunner.ps1 -RunnerRoot C:/src/quic-interop/quic-interop-runner -LocalRole client -ImplementationSlot chrome -PeerImplementationSlots ngtcp2 -TestCases handshake -ArtifactsRoot .artifacts/interop-runner/ngtcp2-expanded-pn-fix -RunnerTimeoutSeconds 180
status_summary: Passed locally on 2026-05-19: captured interop replay suite 29/29, and Incursa.Quic client versus ngtcp2 server handshake rerun succeeded with a 1024-byte response read before peer FIN.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This verification closes the representative ngtcp2 application-response liveness gap. It does not promote all upstream implementations, all testcases, or HTTP/3 support.
